detail.reading: that extra read lands on an EMPTY quadrant in this clone — 664's 22 pe:none elements are all non-controls, so the recommendation is insurance, not a fixed defect

no-control-in-the-population-has-pointer.note: record this BEFORE building on 677's recommendation

the-5x5-grid-probe-sees-four-to-thirty-t.note: centre sees 1-6, the grid sees 27-33, at every cell

detail.thirdState: gridCentre is null when the control's centre lies outside the viewport, so the grid never samples it. That is `missing`, not `measured false` — and the centre probe does return false there.

the-two-probe-paths-agree-on-every-sampl.note: an instrument cross-check: the two are different expressions in the page. The first version of this check compared null against false and reported a disagreement that was really an unmeasured point

every-missed-control-has-a-named-coverer.note: 0.12/0.20/0.40 are 3/25, 5/25, 10/25 — the coverers are axis-aligned rects covering whole grid columns, not jitter

detail.sourceFact: src/components/director/DirectorInspector.tsx:172-175 records the source's number box as `h-full min-w-0 flex-1 pl-6 pr-0` with the comment 'pl-6 让开轴片'. The padding makes room; the chips still sit INSIDE the <input>'s box, so 40% of it is covered.

the-nine-inspector-number-boxes-are-40-p.note: the centre probe cannot see it — the chips are on the left, the centre is clear

detail.why: 667's census additionally requires an enclosing pointer-events:none layer, so it is a subset of the centre probe's population, which is itself a subset of the grid's

667s-population-is-the-smallest-of-the-t.note: three probe rules, three populations, one order
